To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we established a machine learning pipeline to generate feature vectors on the basis of ontological annotations and applied them to similarity search on biodiversity knowledge graphs; (2) the pipeline can be used to successfully cluster species for life form (tree vs. perennial plant etc.) on the basis of trait ontological annotations.

machine learning based approaches can be used for semantic similarity search on biodiversity knowledge graphs and can be applied to the identification of ecotype and life forms of wild plant species based on their trait annotations.

we have shown that it is possible to use a combination of ontology based feature learning and machine learning to cluster biodiversity entities in vector space.
